newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-AssiDoman supports brighter forestry trend.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-AssiDoman supports brighter forestry trend.

text.p: Swedish forestry company AssiDoman on Tuesday posted slightly higher than expected earnings for the first half of the year, supporting growing sentiment that prospects for the industry are brightening.
Forestry shares rose in Stockholm and Helsinki, boosted by recent upgrades and advances in U.S. paper stocks overnight, and AssiDoman reporting earnings in the upper range of forecasts, brokers said.

AssiDoman posted a profit after financial items of 859 million crowns ($107.2 million) which was over market expectations of 819 million crowns but 30 percent lower than the 1.23 billion the group posted in the first half of 1996.
It said it expected a continued strengthening of trends in the forestry industry in 1997 and said the positive market development for paper and carton board especially kraftliner was continuing.

"The view confirms that the industry trends in pulp and paper are gaining a bit of momentum and that the cycle is beginning to show better trends as we head into the second half of the year," Goldman Sachs analyst Hakan Ostling said.

AssiDoman's managing director Lennart Ahlgren told a news conference the improving performance was expected to continue and that trend was strengthened by the fact that turnover in the second quarter of 1997 was 40 percent better a year ago.
"The rolling 12 month curve has moved and is continuing up," Ahlgren said, adding "the curve is improving but by how much we don't know."

Finland's UPM-Kymmene and Enso traded in record territory, while in Sweden the forestry sector index was up 2.28 percent at 1040 GMT while the general index was 0.3 percent higher. AssiDoman shares were four higher at 237 crowns.

Rival Swedish forestry company Stora last week said its profit rose to 1.22 billion crowns for the first half of the year, also above expectations of 1.13 billion, saying the situation looked better than at any point during the 1990s.
Finland's Metsa-Serla last week reported first half earnings near the highest forecast in a Reuters poll.
Analysts said AssiDoman's annoucement that it expected prices of unbleached kraftliner to be lifted by eight to ten percent around October 1 could boost the 1997 result.

"AssiDoman points to strength especially in kraftliner and cartonboard...demand is firmer and they see scope for better pricing in the second half which could pave the way for stronger earnings," Ostling said.
Ostling said he may revise 1997 earnings estimates upward.
AssiDoman said demand for sawn timber remained positive and there was a weak upturn for the pulp market.

AssiDoman said it could put more than eight billion crowns into investments this year with the possibility of another fairly large acquisition this autumn, adding the purchase would focus on corrugated board and be in western Europe.
But this did not come as a surprise, analysts said.
"I don't think that's something people get very excited about," said Claes Vikbladh, analyst at Nordiska Fondkommission.
"I think people would rather see the company distributing earnings to shareholders rather than continuing to invest large amounts."
Out of Sweden's other forestry companies, SCA is due to release earnings on August 13 and MoDo on August 14.
UPM-Kymmene is due to report first half earnings on Thursday at 0500 GMT and Enso early on Wednesday.
-- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1003 ($ = 8.015 Swedish Crowns)
